subject: wss://stream.data.alpaca.markets/v2/iex
readThisFirst: THESE ARE NOT RAW VENDOR BODIES. `src/fixtures/alpaca/` holds recorded HTTP
responses, byte-for-byte as the vendor sent them. This corpus does not, and the
two must never be read as equivalent evidence.
Story 3.1's 31 socket captures were deleted on 2026-09-18 with the harness that
took them — always the plan (ALPACA.md §11: run it, record the findings, delete
it). What survives is LIVE-DATA.md, which recorded the frames in prose.
So every fixture here carries a `provenance` tier saying how far it is from the
wire. Trust them in that order and no further.

provenanceTiers.raw: Bytes the vendor sent, stored unaltered. NOTHING in this corpus is raw.
provenanceTiers.transcribed: Copied character-for-character out of a LIVE-DATA.md section that quoted the frame verbatim. The bytes are the vendor's; the chain of custody is a document rather than a capture file.
provenanceTiers.reconstructed: The frame's SHAPE is inferred from a transcribed frame and its FIELD VALUES from a measured table. Nobody has seen these exact bytes on a wire. See `knownWeakness` below.

frames.what: The server's unsolicited greeting, 2 ms after the upgrade. The ONLY unsolicited frame in the whole handshake capture — every other frame is a reply, checked with a three-second quiet window as the control.
Reply to `auth`, +273 ms. THIS, not `onopen`, is what connected state is driven by (§4.5).
Reply to subscribe, +261 ms. The server echoes the FULL held state, not the delta.
Reply to unsubscribe-everything, +256 ms. An acknowledgement with no `bars` key at all — a parser reading `bars` unconditionally breaks here.

`ZZQQTESTX` SILENTLY ACCEPTED and echoed as held. Alpaca does not validate symbols, so an acknowledgement is NOT evidence a symbol exists — validation against our own universe must happen before the frame is sent.
Two symbols held after a second subscribe. Also the answer to an unsubscribe of a symbol never held: accepted, state unchanged.

FIVE distinct causes produce this one frame: an empty symbol list, a subscribe with no channel, an unknown channel, a real channel on the wrong stream, and an unknown action. The empty-list case is the one a filter matching nothing produces. §8.3: this is the one error an operator can act on differently, because it means our frame was wrong rather than our identity.
60 trade symbols refused. THE CONTROL for the whole cap measurement — it is what proves the instrument could see a cap at all, which is why bars being exempt is a finding rather than an absence.

The `sip` refusal, arriving at AUTHENTICATION as a frame, +255 ms — after which the server leaves the socket OPEN and silent. A client keying connected state off `onopen` reports a healthy SIP connection indefinitely.

Sent to the NEWCOMER 233 ms after it authenticates; it is closed 9,964 ms later while the incumbent keeps its socket and all 518 subscriptions. A rolling deploy has two processes alive by design and the arriving one is ours, so this is a fact about EVERY deploy. Wait and retry, never fatal.

BYTE-IDENTICAL for a wrong key, a wrong secret and no credential at all. An operator log cannot distinguish them and must not claim to; the honest sentence names the class. The socket stays OPEN after it (§8.4).

A real minute bar. `t` marks the START of the interval — confirmed against an HTTP control in §7.3 rather than assumed, and a stream that disagreed would put every live bar a minute out on every surface at once.

frames.from: envelope: LIVE-DATA.md §7.3 (verbatim). Field values: §7.8's measured table.
frames.observed: the BEHAVIOUR was observed 2026-09-16; these exact bytes were not
frames.what: An `updatedBars` revision of the bar above, changing `v` and `n` only — §7.8's measured majority case (11 of 14). Revisions arrive 29.1-30.1 s after the bar they correct (§14.1, n=68).
inferred: That a `u` frame carries the same field set as a `b` frame. LIVE-DATA.md records what `u` frames CHANGED, never their bytes.

frames.from: envelope: LIVE-DATA.md §7.3 (verbatim). Delta modelled on §7.8's SPY row (c 758.85 -> 758.81).
frames.observed: the BEHAVIOUR was observed 2026-09-16; these exact bytes were not
frames.what: A revision that moves the CLOSE — the case that matters, measured at 35.3% of revisions at universe scale (§14.1), where NONE changed nothing at all. This is the frame that makes ignoring `u` mean being quietly wrong by a few cents for ever.
inferred: That a `u` frame carries the same field set as a `b` frame.

heartbeat.what: The server's 54 s ping is a WebSocket CONTROL frame, not a JSON payload, so it cannot be a file in this corpus. `ws@8` surfaces it as a `ping` event and Node's built-in WebSocket cannot see it at all (§4.6) — which is what decides the library.
heartbeat.measured: 53.96-54.85 s across 82 intervals, on a socket subscribed to nothing as much as on one subscribed to all 518 (§6.3). A property of the CONNECTION, not the subscription.
heartbeat.testedBy: stream-connection.test.ts, which takes a `heartbeat` event rather than a frame.

close.what: A close is an event, not a payload. All five observed causes produce code 1006 with an empty reason (§8.5), so there is nothing to store.
close.discriminator: The close LATENCY: ~1 ms our own link went, ~240 ms a live socket answering, ~6 s the server closing a rude client, ~10 s a refused duplicate, ~30 s ws@8 timing out on a corpse.

knownWeakness.what: NO VERBATIM `u` FRAME EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THIS REPOSITORY.
knownWeakness.why: LIVE-DATA.md §7.8 recorded what the 14 revisions CHANGED — symbol, bar timestamp, lag, fields — and never quoted a frame. The captures that held the bytes were deleted with the harness on 2026-09-18, and a `u` frame only occurs during a live session, so it could not be re-recorded on the day this corpus was built (02:28 ET, market shut).
knownWeakness.riskIfWrong: Only the ENVELOPE is at risk, and it is bounded: if a real `u` carries a different field set, 3.2.4's mapper is wrong about `u` and right about everything else. The SEMANTICS the fixtures encode — a revision supersedes a (symbol, minute) rather than adding to it — are measured and are not in doubt.
knownWeakness.owner: Task 3.2.5, which is the first task that opens a real socket.
knownWeakness.trigger: The first `u` frame 3.2.5 observes during a live session. Record it verbatim, replace both reconstructed fixtures, and re-tier them to `transcribed`.
